title: Sizes, SameLine, Spacing and Groups
summary: ImGui places widgets with a **cursor** that moves down after each one. This lesson shows how to control it - `SameLine`, item widths, spacing, indentation, groups, alignment and disabled sections - so a tool's window reads cleanly at any font size.
markdown:
## The cursor

Every window has a layout **cursor**. Each widget is placed at the cursor, then the cursor moves to the start of the next line. That is why widgets stack vertically by default. Everything in this lesson changes where the cursor goes, or how wide the next widget is.

## SameLine

```cpp-norun
ImGui::Text("Stones:");
ImGui::SameLine();                    // the next widget goes to the right of the last one
ImGui::Text("%d", count);
ImGui::SameLine(200.0f);              // ...at x = 200 from the window's left edge
ImGui::Button("Add");
ImGui::SameLine(0.0f, 2.0f);          // default position, but only 2 pixels of spacing
ImGui::Button("-");
```

## Widths

By default, widgets with a frame (sliders, inputs, combos) take about two thirds of the window width, leaving room for the label on the right. Change it:

```cpp-norun
ImGui::SetNextItemWidth(120.0f);                 // the next widget only
ImGui::DragFloat("Mass", &mass);

ImGui::PushItemWidth(-FLT_MIN);                  // all following widgets: fill to the right edge
ImGui::InputText("##notes", &notes);             // (hide the label with ##, or it would be cut off)
ImGui::PopItemWidth();

ImGui::PushItemWidth(ImGui::GetFontSize() * 10); // ten "M" widths: scales with the font
```

Prefer sizes based on `GetFontSize()`, `GetFrameHeight()` and `GetContentRegionAvail()` over fixed pixel numbers, so the tool still looks right when someone raises the font size or the display scale.

```cpp-norun
const float avail = ImGui::GetContentRegionAvail().x;            // width left on this line
ImGui::Button("Half", ImVec2(avail * 0.5f, 0));                  // 0 height = the normal height
```

## Spacing, separators, indentation

```cpp-norun
ImGui::Spacing();                 // a little vertical space
ImGui::Separator();               // a horizontal line
ImGui::SeparatorText("Physics");  // a line with a title
ImGui::Indent();                  // move the left edge right (by the style's indent width)
ImGui::Text("indented");
ImGui::Unindent();
ImGui::Dummy(ImVec2(0, 20));      // an invisible widget that takes space
ImGui::NewLine();                 // move to the next line, like pressing Enter
```

## Groups

A **group** makes several widgets act as one item for layout: you can put the whole group on the same line as something else, and `IsItemHovered` asks about the whole group.

```cpp-norun
ImGui::BeginGroup();
ImGui::Text("Player");
ImGui::Text("HP %d", hp);
ImGui::Text("MP %d", mp);
ImGui::EndGroup();
ImGui::SameLine();                // the next group sits to the right of the whole first group
ImGui::BeginGroup();
ImGui::Text("Enemy");
ImGui::Text("HP %d", enemyHp);
ImGui::EndGroup();
```

## Alignment

ImGui lays text from the top of the line. Next to a framed widget (a button, an input) plain text looks too high. Call `ImGui::AlignTextToFramePadding()` before such text to line it up with the frames on the same line.

To right-align something, move the cursor yourself:

```cpp-norun
const float w = ImGui::CalcTextSize("Delete").x + ImGui::GetStyle().FramePadding.x * 2;
ImGui::SameLine(ImGui::GetContentRegionMax().x - w);
ImGui::Button("Delete");
```

`CalcTextSize` measures text with the current font. The practice uses that kind of measurement to lay out a row of buttons.

## Disabled sections

```cpp-norun
ImGui::BeginDisabled(!level.loaded);    // greyed out and not interactive while no level is loaded
if (ImGui::Button("Save")) saveLevel();
ImGui::EndDisabled();
```

Better than hiding the button: the user sees it exists and why it cannot be used yet (add a tooltip, lesson 4.02).

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Fixed pixel sizes everywhere
> They break at other font sizes and display scales. Measure from the font and the available width.

> [!warning] A full-width widget with a visible label
> The label is pushed off the right edge. Hide it with ## and put a Text in front instead.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? How does ImGui decide where a widget goes?
+ At the window's layout cursor, which moves to the next line after each widget unless SameLine or other layout calls change it
- At a position you must give every widget, measured from the window's top-left corner
- In a grid of rows and columns that ImGui works out from all the widgets at the end of the frame
> Widgets stack vertically because the cursor moves down after each one. Layout happens immediately, widget by widget.

? Why measure sizes from the font and the available region?
- Because ImGui ignores sizes given in pixels
+ So the layout adapts to other font sizes, display scaling and window sizes
- Because measured sizes make widgets draw faster
> A fixed 120 pixels looks cramped once someone raises the font size; GetFontSize() * 10 grows with it.

? What does a group do?
- It draws a frame around several widgets with a title, like a group box
- It gives every widget inside it the same ID, so they share state
+ It makes several widgets act as one item for layout and item queries
> After EndGroup, SameLine puts the next widget to the right of the whole group, and IsItemHovered asks about all of it.

? Which call puts the next widget to the right of the previous one?
- ImGui::NewLine()
+ ImGui::SameLine()
- ImGui::Indent()
> SameLine moves the cursor back up to the end of the last item. Indent moves the left edge of following lines.

? What does a width of -FLT_MIN mean for PushItemWidth?
- No width at all, so the widgets are hidden
- The default width, about two thirds of the window
+ Fill up to the right edge of the window
> It is ImGui's idiom for "all the space that is left". Hide the label with ## or it is pushed off the edge.

? Why use BeginDisabled instead of hiding a button?
- Disabled buttons cost less to draw than hidden ones do
- Hidden buttons still receive clicks, disabled ones do not
+ The user sees the action exists and that it cannot be used right now
> Make it clear why with a tooltip.
```
ideas:
- Lay out a "Player" panel with a label column and value column using `SameLine(x)` with an x based on `GetFontSize()`.
- Put three buttons right-aligned at the bottom of a window: "Cancel", "Apply", "OK".
- Grey out the save button while nothing has changed.
